title: Hermetica, Vol. 3
author: Walter Scott (ed)
description: Hermetica, Volume 3, edited by Walter Scott (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1926), the third volume of Scott's edition of the Greek and Latin writings ascribed to Hermes Trismegistus. Where the first volume contains the texts of the Corpus Hermeticum and Asclepius, Volume 3 contains Scott's notes and commentary on the Latin Asclepius and on the Hermetic excerpts preserved by Stobaeus, including the Kore Kosmou (Virgin of the World), a mythic dialogue between Isis and Horus on the creation of souls and the origin of humanity. Scott's extensive commentary discusses textual problems, parallels in Plato, the Stoics, Philo and Gnostic writers, and the dating and milieu of the treatises. It is a scholarly reference for close study of Hermetic doctrine, to be used alongside the text volume.
